title: Due-and-Payable Retention Payoff Calculation Clause
content:
# Due-and-payable retention payoff — calculation clause (Payoff and Loan Satisfaction)

HUD's due-and-payable payoff rule lets the borrower satisfy the loan for the lesser of the balance owed and 95 percent of the current appraised value. On the payoff case of a Borrower Voluntary Payoff requested by the borrower of record on a loan whose maturity case is due and payable, in its extension period or referred to foreclosure, the approved retention payoff is the lesser of the retention balance figure and the due-and-payable value cap, rounded half up to the cent and only at that last step.

1. **Appraised value basis.** The appraised value on the loan's maturity case, which must be dated within that case plan's appraisal validity period in months.
2. **Due-and-payable value cap.** 95 percent of the appraised value basis, rounded half up to the cent.
3. **Retention balance figure.** The statement balance the payoff case carries plus five resolution charges (the called-due appraisal charge, the replacement appraisal charge, the foreclosure charge, the property securing charge and the notice postage charge), less the prompt-decision credit. The charges are added and the credit deducted before the lesser of the two figures is taken.
4. **Charges and credit.** The called-due appraisal charge is USD 475.00; the replacement appraisal charge, the foreclosure charge, the property securing charge, the notice postage charge and the prompt-decision credit are each 0.00.
5. **Result.** The lesser of item 3 and item 2, rounded half up to the cent.

### Two hypothetical cases

| Hypothetical input | Case A | Case B |
|---|---|---|
| Statement balance on the case | USD 180000.00 | USD 180000.00 |
| Appraised value basis | USD 185000.00 | USD 200000.00 |
| Value cap (95 percent) | USD 175750.00 | USD 190000.00 |
| Retention balance figure | USD 180475.00 | USD 180475.00 |
| Approved retention payoff | USD 175750.00 | USD 180475.00 |

In case A the cap is the lesser; in case B the retention balance figure is. Both cases are invented for the illustration.
